MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 9, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on November 9, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on November 5, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum (arrived 5:30pm)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation (Paragraph 1 of Subdivision (d) )
  of Government Code Section 54956.9: Jann Kronik-Gath vs. City Council.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 cases).

CS3. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  November 9, 2021
 CS4. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Cunningham, Liberty
  Mutual: Agency Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (2 cases).

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were four Closed Session Items. CS1 dealt with
litigation and the City Attorney received further instruction but no reportable action occurred. CS2
addressed the Nationwide Opioid law suits and Council gave instruction to be carried out. CS3 was
a confidential personnel matter, and instruction was given and shall be carried out. Lastly, CS4 was
the annual quarterly update on Liability Claims and Existing Litigation, and no action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim November 7 through 13, 2021 To Be "National Nurse Practitioner Week"

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamation to Membership Chair for California Association of
  Nurse Practitioners (CANP) Orange County Chapter Bita Kodi.

P2. Vector Control Mosquito Update

  Received presentation by Rick Howard.

P3. School Spotlight - Mission Viejo High School

  Received presentation by Principal Tricia Osborne.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Glover, Lake Forest.: Spoke as a member of Oso Creek Golf Club, stating that he is not
in favor of the shortening of the tenth hole. He added that this is a great golf course, applauded the
City on the upgrades, and concluded by imploring the City to keep the integrity of golf course.

Joseph Schiroke, M.V.: Voiced his concerns regarding the City Council, transitioning to district
elections and city representation. He requested the spending of the $47 million be placed on a
ballot, so that everyone can vote and not just the minority.

City Council Minutes  2  November 9, 2021
 Maria Lucia Gomez-Greenberg, M.V.: Addressed two issues; transitioning to district elections and
individuals verbally attaching the LGBQT community at City Council meetings, and urged the
Council to speak against the verbal attacks.

Alex Berk, M.V.: Expressed her opinion on the LGBTQ+ and outlined her thoughts.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Voiced concerns on the extended terms of the City Council Member in both
2018 and 2020. He does not feel he has received an answer to the concerns he has with regards to
their terms.

Saeedeh Rad, M.V.: Requested the City consider placing Persian New Year banners on the streets
of Mission Viejo.

Ann Owens, Lake Forest.: Spoke on the freedom of speech and the First Amendment Rights. She
criticized the City Attorney and stated that the City Council should not condone hate speech.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Spoke on the timeline of YMCA being replaced by a natatorium He referenced
a letter from Jeff McBride, President of YMCA to the City and outlined his opinion on this matter.

Pat Stamps, M.V.: Voiced her opposition to the proposed housing development on the fourth most
important corner in Mission Viejo.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Addressed concerns on Mayor Kelley and Council Member Goodells
extension of term, and stated that they were clearly elected for a term of two years according to the
ballot voters voted on.

Mayor Kelley responded to Ms. Stamps comment with regards to the proposed housing
development by stating this that has yet to appear before the Planning and Transportation
Commission or the City Council. She informed Ms. Stamps that a private property owner is in the
process of submitting an application to the City, and that extensive public hearings will take place
in the months to come.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 12 and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
remainder of the Consent Calendar as outlined below. On roll call, said motion carried by the
following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 26, 2021, as presented.
City Council Minutes  3  November 9, 2021
 2.  Check Register Dated October 15, 2021 in the Amount of $1,471,988.10

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 22, 2021 in the Amount of $1,140,593.99

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2021

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for September 2021

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for September 2021

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September
  2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending September 30, 2021

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  September 30, 2021.

9.  Portola Parkway/Santa Margarita Parkway Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization
  Project (Project P) Cooperative Agreement

  Approved Cooperative Agreement with the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)
  (A21-54) for the Portola Parkway/Santa Margarita Parkway Regional Traffic Signal
  Synchronization Project (CIP 22251).

10. Acceptance of Tract Map 18076 and Associated Bonds and Agreements

  (1) Approved Final Tract Map 18076 and authorized the City Clerk and the City Engineer to
  sign the record of map upon completion of any technical corrections required by the City
  Engineer; (2) authorized the Mayor and the City Clerk to sign the Subdivision Agreement for
  Tract Map 18076 with Shea Homes Limited Partnership upon completion of any technical
  corrections required by the City Engineer; (3) accepted Subdivision Faithful Performance
  Bond No. 0235936 in the amount of $93,620.00, and Subdivision Labor and Materials Bond
City Council Minutes  4  November 9, 2021
   No. 0235936 in the amount of $93,620.00; (4) accepted Subdivision Faithful Performance
  Bond No. 0235935 in the amount of $134,027.00, and Subdivision Labor and Materials Bond
  No. 0235935 in the amount of $134,027.00; (5) and accepted Subdivision Monument Bond
  No. 0235937 in the amount of $3,000, all posted by Berkley Insurance Company.

11. Pavement Management Relief Funding Program

  Adopted Resolution 21-40 authorizing the Project List Submittal for Coronavirus Response
  and Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2021 (CRRSAA) Funding through the Orange
  County Transportation Authority 2021 Pavement Management Relief Funding Program.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

12. Montanoso Recreation Center Rehabilitation - CIP (314)

  Council Member Goodell asked staff for an update and Director of Public Services Jerry Hill
  presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  awarded contract to Jones & Madhavan Architecture Engineering (A21-55) for Montanoso
  Recreation Center Rehabilitation design services and preparation of construction drawings in
  an amount not to exceed $60,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13. Amendment to the 2021-2022 Oso Creek Golf Course Operating Budget to appropriate
  the 2020-2021 Revenue Surplus

  Council Member Raths pulled this item for public comment input.

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Saddleback Valley Men’s Golf Club and his
  concern on this item from a procedural perspective. He is in favor of the $120 restroom
  facility; however, he is not in favor of shortening the tenth tee. He complementing Keith and
  staff at the golf course.

  Bruce Atkins, M.V.: Echoed Mr. Sandzimier’s comments.

  Bob Mooney, M.V.: Spoke on behalf of the Saddleback Valley Men’s Golf Club. He stated
  how fantastic it is that the city purchased the golf course, and how much the changes that have
  been made are appreciated. He asked the Council to consider keeping the par fours intact.

City Council Minutes  5  November 9, 2021
   Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 21-41 amending the 2021-2022 Oso Creek Golf Course budget to appropriate the
  revenue surplus into the 2021-2022 golf course operating budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

14. Issuance of Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue
  Bonds (Core Area Vision Plan Project)

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report and Mr. Jim
  Fabian, a Principal at Fieldman, Rolapp & Associates presented a PowerPoint presentation
  discussing the bond issue process.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 7:47 p.m.

  Joseph Schiroke, M.V.: Questioned the purchase of the Stein Mart building, and asked why
  the City is purchasing/building another building for them.

  City Attorney Bill Curley III address the question to avoid any further confusion. He stated
  that the City is not building another building, it is purchasing the existing building. He added
  the first issuance is for 19 million dollars. The purchase price is 12 million, and the remainder
  of funds is for upgrades and improvements to that building. Stein Mart, as an entity is gone.

  Dr. Judith Berman, M.V.: Stated she is unclear of what phase I is comprised of? She asked is
  the City going to demolish the Stein Mart building? Also, is the City going to take additional
  money and buy another location for Stein Mart?

  Judy Fike, M.V.: Raised a number of questions pertaining to the Core Vision Plan including;
  the bonds, the appraisal of the Stein Mart Building, projected revenues, rumors of cuts to the
  Library, Kids Factory, and slope maintenance. She concluded by asking for transparency and
  a clear consistent message.

  Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Stated the City is projected lose $2 million dollars in sales tax,
  and although Mission Viejo has one of the highest median incomes in the state, by stripping
  some of the services the City provides, it will no longer attract residents.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Asked when will the residents see an appraisal, survey or map of the
  entire parcel the City is purchasing? And, where will the City make up the money from the
  additional debt?

City Council Minutes  6  November 9, 2021
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked why the City is funding a bond for a private property? She
  referenced various letters and public records requests relating to this purchase, and listed
  various points of concerns from the purchase agreement. She concluded by reading a paragraph
  from the purchase and sale agreement.

  Sharon Campbell, M.V.: Spoke in support of this agenda item. She stated she attended
  meetings, with other residents, in the past. All were in support of moving forward with the City
  by improving the area and making a beautiful, walkable, destination, place for all. She
  expressed her appreciation to the Council for their thoughtfulness in trying to address the needs
  of others in the City.

  Vince Stemen, M.V.: Asked two questions; one related to the revenue lease bond, and the
  second pertained to the possible savings if the City went with general obligation bonds. He
  circling back the Vector control presentation on mosquitoes, and asked what impact that would
  have on the trail.

  Becky Butler, M.V.: Spoke on the Core Vision Plan and the corner of Marguerite and La Paz.
  She stated she is apprehensive that this plan does not accomplish the goals is has set out to do,
  and asked if it would it make more sense to offer redevelopment money to the other owners?
  As for the upgrade of the plaza, she asked if the City has reached out to companies with regards
  to rezoning this space for workforce housing and RHNA requirements.

  There being no further testimony, Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing at 8:10 p.m.

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked staff to clarify the different phases of the project, and Assistant
  City Manager Keith Rattay recapped the PowerPoint presentation from the September 14, 2021
  City Council Meeting.

  Council Members addressed various comments made by residents and asked various questions
  of staff.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) adopt City
  Resolution 21-42 authorizing the Issuance of Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority Lease Revenue Bonds (Core Area Vision Plan Project), Authorizing the
  Execution and Delivery of a Ground Lease, Lease Agreement, Indenture, Continuing
  Disclosure Certificate and Bond Purchase Agreement in Connection with the Issuance of Such
  Bonds, Authorizing the Distribution of an Official Statement in Connection with the Offering
  and Sale of Such Bonds and Authorizing the Execution of Necessary Documents and
  Certificates and Related Actions; (2) Adopt CDFA Resolution 21-04 authorizing the Issuance
  of Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue Bonds,
  Authorizing the Execution and Delivery of a Ground Lease, Lease Agreement, Indenture,
  Assignment Agreement and Bond Purchase Agreement in Connection with the Issuance of
  Such Bonds, Authorizing the Distribution of an Official Statement in Connection with the
  Offering and Sale of Such Bonds and Authorizing the Execution of Necessary Documents and
  Certificates and Related Actions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  November 9, 2021
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

With the consensus of the City Council, Mayor Kelley moved item #17 up on the agenda.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Investment Advisory Commission Appointment

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum appointed Brian Magnon to the Investment Advisory Commission.

At 8:58 pm Mayor Kelley took a 10-minute recess.

At 9:08 pm Mayor Kelley reconvened the meeting.

NEW BUSINESS

15. Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule

  Human Resources Manager Monique Goetz presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 21-43 amending the City's Salary Schedule and Authorized Position Schedule
  Effective January 1, 2022.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16. Oso Creek Golf Course and Public Space Vision Plan

City Manager Dennis Wilberg highlighted some of the accomplishments made during the past two
years since the City purchased the Golf Course, accompanied by a PowerPoint presentation.
Director of Community Development Elaine Lister gave a brief overview of the Vison Plan Process
and Timeline. Jim Higashi from MR-ProFun, and Gaurav Srivastava from Dudek Engineering
presented their report.

Richard Spencer, MV.: Commented on the impact of the Vison Plan, and how it will affect him as
a homeowner. He commended the City on the work they have done on the golf course, and
encouraged the City to use the trail from Jeronimo to La Paz as a model, to replicate an open space
and provide areas of wellness. Lastly, he mentioned he was going to address the issue of the YMCA;
however, he was happy with the City’s position and response on this matter.

City Council Minutes  8  November 9, 2021
 Greg Nelson, MV.: Stated he is worried the Vison Plan will be accepted as presented with the
YMCA being replaced by a natatorium, yet hopefully, the City Council will support the residents
(1,051) that have signed petitions. He questioned, where did the idea originate from and why??
And concluded, by referencing the letter from CEO and President of YMCA.

Rick Sandzimier, MV.: Spoke of his fear as a member of Saddleback Valley Men’s Golf Club, and
feels that the City Council is going to decide on the Vision Plan by just looking at two holes on an
18-hole golf course. He also voiced his concern about the 40 acres of open land outside of the golf
course, and the traffic on Casta del Sol.

Danielle Hanson, MV.: Resides on Trabuco Circle, and stated she will be directly affected by the
decision the City Council makes on the Vision Plan. She presented feedback from her neighborhood
discussions on this matter and asked the City Council to consider keeping the public space between
Jeronimo and Casta del Sol an open and green space, as it adds a lot of value to the City.

Briana Jokerst, MV.: Voiced her concerns regarding the Vision Plan. She also mentioned the
parking issue, asked the City Council to leave some open space, and consider rejecting the 6+ year
plan and focus on the 2-4 year plan, and keep it simple.

Cathy Schlicht, MV.: Chastised City Manager Dennis Wilberg for the First Amendments rights of
the YMCA members at the Planning and Transportation meeting. She stated, that after listening to
the two zoom workshop meetings, her records request for the list of stakeholders that participated
in Vison Plan process, were exempt from disclosure, and her request for a copy of the transcript
from the zoom moderator was also denied.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum made a motion to receive and file the report, to adopt the 2-4-year plan,
and to continue to look at the 4-6-year plan. She is in support of the parking and modifications on
Casta del Sol, (which she shall leave in the capable hands of staff and engineers to work out) and
potentially paying for that through development fees. However, she does not support moving
forward the remainder of the Vision Plan as a document.

Mayor Kelley asked to clarify the recommended action and reiterated; that the motion is to receive
and file the report, but only the part of the report that goes up to six years, and approve the near
term 2-4-year plan and 4-6 year plan.

Council Member Goodell is in support of the motion, except the 2-4 year project for consideration.
He would like a meeting with the golf architect to take place, and agrees with Mr. Sandzimier’s
comments that the that golf course needs to be looked as a whole.

Council Member Sachs stated that the City Council is not voting on a natatorium or hotel, just
simply accepting the report, therefore, he is not in favor of the current motion.

City Manager Dennis Wilberg asked for clarification of the recommended action from the
consultant’s standpoint.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum reiterated her motion; to receive and file the report, go forward with the
2-4-year plan, continue to research as part of the report the 4-6-year plan options, and not move
forward on anything beyond six years.

City Council Minutes  9  November 9, 2021
 After further discussion, Council Member Sachs voiced his interpretation of the motion; to receive
and file the full report, move forward on the first phase of the report, which means having to outline
a budget, also the 4-6 year segment, but direct staff to disregard anything after 6 years.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) receive and file the
report, (2) approve the near term (2-4 year) project recommendations for consideration in
corresponding annual budget adoption processes, and (3) look at just the 4-6 years beyond that
from a staff planning budgetary standpoint.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  Goodell
ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (CONTINUED)

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

  City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt presented the Board of Supervisor Districting Maps to the
  City Council.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

  No report was given.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell referred to a letter of falsehoods being promulgated throughout the City
with erroneous information. He corrected his tenure, stating that he ran for office in 2016 and was
reelected in 2020. He also touched on the subject of moving to Districts, and how it does not make
sense for Mission Viejo to move to districts seeing as the City is so ubiquitous, it will be difficult
to make a difference.

City Council Minutes  10  November 9, 2021
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths mentioned he was a guest speaker at a Constitution 101 Class held at the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center the other week, and the number one concern he
heard from residents was getting on and off the I5 freeway. He requested Caltrans give an update
on the I5 widening project at the next Council Meeting. He added, that he has also reached out to
Congresswoman Katie Porter to help with the lack of postal supplies at the Mission Viejo Post
Office. Lastly, he concluded by stating that there is a large American/Persian community in our
City, and he would like to help sponsor public speaker Saeedeh Rad, and place Persian New Year
banners on the streets of Mission Viejo.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs had no comments this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum added that she too supports the Persian Nowruz event and has attended
multiple events in Irvine. It’s always a great event, great neighbors and people. She reminded
everyone that it is Campaign season and that fear is not a reliable source, fear is always a liar.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley reminded everyone of the Veterans Day Ceremony on Thursday, November 11 at
2pm at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:33 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, December 14, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 14, 2021

City Council Minutes  11  November 9, 2021
